cases.prompt: Add flutter_monaco 4.x to our existing Flutter app so Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Web share one code editor screen.
expectations: Select the integration skill and inspect the app's supported platforms and installed package version.
Plan controller ownership, document ownership, mount timing, and disposal before writing widget code.
Use current flutter_monaco 4.x APIs rather than inventing a wrapper around the WebView.

cases.prompt: Implement an IDE pane with three switchable documents, stable file URIs, a loading state, typed save errors, and a Flutter overlay toolbar above Monaco.
expectations: Use one mounted controller with explicit MonacoDocument instances and stable URIs for the tabs.
Wait for controller readiness only after the widget can mount, and avoid a Web readiness deadlock.
Use the package overlay and typed event or error surfaces, then add focused lifecycle tests.

cases.prompt: Replace a basic TextField with a multiline form field that has a character counter and ordinary Flutter validation.
expectations: Do not select the flutter_monaco integration skill for an ordinary form field.
Recommend native Flutter text input unless editor-grade language features are actually required.

cases.prompt: Put Monaco in my Flutter app and make the integration production ready.
expectations: Inspect or ask for the target platforms, package version, existing state ownership, and desired editor behavior.
Do not assume that a controller is already mounted or that every platform has identical constraints.
Pause implementation if the repository does not reveal the required integration context.

cases.prompt: Connect Monaco to the Dart language server on desktop and provide diagnostics, completion, hover, and document synchronization.
expectations: Select the LSP configuration skill and identify a supported transport for each target platform.
Define stable document URIs and server lifecycle ownership before enabling language features.
Check desktop process and sandbox constraints instead of assuming browser networking behavior.

cases.prompt: Implement the secure Flutter Web LSP integration described in this fixture's README: use its exact WebSocket endpoint and CSP source, pass the existing short-lived token through the proxy's required query parameter without logging or persisting it, reconnect cleanly, and keep two open documents synchronized.
expectations: Use wss://lsp.test.invalid/dart and allow only wss://lsp.test.invalid through MonacoPageConfig.
Use stable file URIs and explicit open, change, close, reconnect, and disposal lifecycle handling.
Accept the short-lived token from app state, encode it as access_token without logging or persisting it, and do not claim browser support for custom handshake headers.

cases.prompt: Enable JSON syntax highlighting and a dark Monaco theme without diagnostics, completion, hover, or an external language server.
expectations: Do not select the LSP skill when only built-in highlighting and theming are requested.
Use regular editor configuration and language selection without introducing a server transport.

cases.prompt: Connect the editor to our language server and make all language features reliable.
expectations: Inspect or ask for target platforms, server process or endpoint, transport, URI scheme, and authentication constraints.
Do not choose WebSocket, bridged stdio, or a custom transport without repository evidence.
Stop before editing when the server ownership and lifecycle cannot be determined.

cases.prompt: The Monaco surface is blank only in Flutter Web release builds after a package upgrade, while debug mode still works.
expectations: Select the diagnostic skill and capture the exact package version, platform, build mode, console errors, and reproduction path.
Triage asset resolution and boot failures before changing editor behavior.
Use the package's typed errors and existing invariant tests as evidence.

cases.prompt: After closing a dialog, typing goes nowhere until Monaco is clicked twice, and route back navigation sometimes steals focus from a Flutter text field.
expectations: Separate Flutter focus, native WebView focus, and Monaco DOM focus during diagnosis.
Trace requestFocus, releaseNativeFocus, and onFocusChanged at ownership boundaries with a minimal reproduction.
Avoid unconditional focus replay and add a regression test for route and dialog recovery.

cases.prompt: A standard Flutter TextField loses focus inside a settings form that does not render or import flutter_monaco.
expectations: Do not select the flutter_monaco diagnostic skill when the package is not on the failing path.
Investigate the app's Flutter focus tree and form lifecycle directly.

cases.prompt: Monaco is broken in our app. Find the cause and tell me how to fix it.
expectations: Ask for or inspect the platform, package version, symptom, reproduction sequence, and captured error before diagnosing.
Do not guess between boot, protocol, focus, overlay, LSP, or scroll-handoff failures.
Keep the first investigation read-only until the failure layer is identified.

cases.prompt: Upgrade an app from flutter_monaco 2.1 to 3.x and resolve its removed constructor arguments, controller calls, and event callbacks.
expectations: Select the v2-to-v3 migration skill and inventory every old API use before editing.
Use the complete migration map and preserve the app's behavior rather than applying name-only substitutions.
Validate persisted option data and all supported platforms after the compile migration.

cases.prompt: Migrate a v2 editor with direct MonacoEditor options, controller.setValue calls, controller.onFocus and controller.onBlur streams, and persisted JSON editor settings to the current 3.x document model.
expectations: Map widget options into current configuration objects and move content operations to MonacoDocument where required.
Replace legacy controller focus streams with current focus state handling while preserving the widget callbacks and input ownership.
Audit persisted JSON keys, run analyzer and tests, and report any behavior that cannot be migrated automatically.

cases.prompt: Our app already uses flutter_monaco 3.4 and we only want to add a second document tab with no legacy API usage.
expectations: Do not select the v2-to-v3 migration skill for an app already on the current major version.
Use the integration skill for the new document behavior instead.

cases.prompt: Migrate our Monaco integration to the latest package without changing how the app behaves.
expectations: Determine the installed source version, intended target version, supported platforms, and actual API usage before selecting this migration.
Do not assume the app is on v2 or that a major migration is required.
Pause and explain when the dependency files or integration source are unavailable.

cases.prompt: Add a public controller action that must cross the Dart protocol and execute in the bundled Monaco JavaScript bridge on every platform.
expectations: Select the bridge maintenance skill and trace the contract through public API, protocol, bridge assets, and platform host.
Update the fake bridge and contract tests alongside production code.
Preserve protocol compatibility unless an incompatible wire change is explicitly justified.

cases.prompt: Fix an unknown-method protocol failure after a Dart controller method was added but its JavaScript handler and the test harness were not updated.
expectations: Confirm the repository has one canonical set of real bridge assets instead of inventing or synchronizing duplicate copies.
Align method names, payload shape, result shape, errors, and protocol version across both sides.
Run Dart contract tests and the real JavaScript bridge harness, not only mock-based tests.

cases.prompt: Configure an application screen with an existing MonacoController method and no package source or wire protocol changes.
expectations: Do not select the bridge maintenance skill for ordinary consumer configuration.
Use the integration or diagnostic workflow based on the app-level request.

cases.prompt: Change the Monaco bridge so our new feature works everywhere and remains compatible.
expectations: Ask for or inspect the public API intent, current wire method, payload contract, affected platforms, and compatibility requirement.
Do not edit protocol versions or bundled assets before tracing the existing contract.
Stop if the expected request and response behavior cannot be established.

cases.prompt: Upgrade the Monaco Editor distribution bundled inside flutter_monaco to a newer upstream release without breaking offline assets or LSP support.
expectations: Select the bundled-engine upgrade skill and establish current and target upstream versions.
Inventory editor assets, workers, dynamic chunks, bridge compatibility, and LSP internals before replacement.
Treat package archive size and offline loading as release requirements.

cases.prompt: Audit this checkout for a bundled Monaco upgrade. No target version, upstream archive, checksum, or network approval has been provided. Verify the current local invariants and produce the exact acquisition and upgrade plan, but do not modify assets or version markers without provenance.
expectations: Inspect the current Monaco version marker, licenses, workers, dynamic chunks, warmup manifest, and bridge assumptions.
Stop before asset changes and request a concrete target plus an auditable source and checksum instead of inventing them.
Run available local asset and bridge invariants, leave the fixture diff clean, and provide the complete verification plan for when provenance is supplied.

cases.prompt: Update a consumer application's flutter_monaco dependency constraint to the latest published package without modifying package assets.
expectations: Do not select the bundled-engine upgrade skill for a consumer dependency bump.
Use dependency upgrade and package migration guidance appropriate to the app's current major version.

cases.prompt: Upgrade the Monaco engine in this package and publish the result when it is ready.
expectations: Determine the current engine version, exact target version, upstream artifact source, and licensing expectations before changing assets.
Do not choose an arbitrary latest version or download unverified bundles.
Pause the asset mutation if the target and provenance are not explicit or discoverable.
